- Overestimate prices after sentiment spikes (especially >0.53) — model tends to overshoot in bullish sentiment periods.
- Underestimate prices during prolonged negative sentiment (sentiment <0.27) — model fails to recognize bearish momentum.
- Lag in price correction: model often delays downward revisions after recent spikes, especially when sentiment turns negative.
- Mean reversion bias: model overreacts to short-term volatility, failing to smoothly revert to historical mean in medium-term forecasts.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts consistently overestimate early-term price peaks (first 5–7 days) and underestimate late-term troughs (last 5–7 days).
- Sentiment-weighted adjustment: if sentiment is >0.44, reduce forecast by 2–5% to avoid overconfidence in bullish signals; if sentiment <0.27, increase forecast by 3–7% to compensate for underestimation.
